native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB: Across the 1985 -> 1996 NLSY79 wealth waves, using NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC respondents (cohort code 3) as the supplied proxy for the 'white' comparison group, median family net wealth in nominal dollars of the survey year is ordered NBNH > BLACK > HISPANIC in every wave, and the disparity between the white-comparison cohort and each minority cohort widens monotonically across the window. The white-comparison median is 2.19x the Black median and 7.00x the Hispanic median in 1985 ($3,500 vs. $1,600 vs. $500; available-case N = 5,774 / 1,699 / 2,631), 2.70x and 8.11x in 1990 ($12,972 vs. $4,800 vs. $1,600; N = 5,336 / 1,528 / 2,431), and 4.35x and 16.62x in 1996 ($42,600 vs. $9,800 vs. $2,563; N = 3,557 / 1,368 / 2,114), so the white-to-Black gap nearly doubles (2.19x -> 4.35x) and the white-to-Hispanic gap more than doubles (7.00x -> 16.62x) over the eleven-year span. A complete-case sensitivity panel restricted to respondents with non-missing wealth in all three waves (N = 5,739; Black 1,084 / Hispanic 1,723 / NBNH 2,932) reproduces the same ordering and the same widening trajectory for both minority contrasts. Because all figures are in the nominal dollars reported at each interview and no CPI/deflator adjustment is applied, part of the nominal widening mechanically reflects economy-wide price and wage growth between 1985 and 1996 rather than only relative shifts in the wealth distribution. Caveats: NBNH is a supplied proxy rather than strictly non-Hispanic white; wealth is family-level not per-capita; cohort is fixed at 1979; headline uses within-wave available cases (complete-case is sensitivity only); the analysis is descriptive on point estimates with no inferential test; and 1996 attrition is mildly differential (~52.7% NBNH vs ~31.7% Black / ~33.3% Hispanic), mitigated but not eliminated by the complete-case panel.

Key columns: 'Racial/ethnic cohort, 1979' (codes 1=BLACK n=2,002; 2=HISPANIC n=3,174; 3=NBNH n=7,510) and 'Family net wealth, 1985' / 'Family net wealth, 1990' / 'Family net wealth, 1996 (key data point)' (the 1996 header carries the literal suffix). 2. Headline — within-wave available case: per-cohort median family net wealth computed on rows with non-missing wealth in that wave (negatives and zeros retained); per-cohort N, P25/P75, share of respondents with non-positive wealth reported alongside. 3. Within-wave ratios: R_black(w) = M_NBNH/M_BLACK, R_hispanic(w) = M_NBNH/M_HISPANIC, with 1/R also reported. 4.
